question.worked_solution:
First, we rewrite the limit as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to -\infty }{2}^{-5x} & ={lim}_{x\to -\infty }{(\frac{1}{2})}^{5x} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to -\infty }{[{(\frac{1}{2})}^{5}]}^{x} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to -\infty }{(\frac{1}{32})}^{x}\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we recall the graph of $y={(\frac{1}{32})}^{x}.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14258364/assets/169fc7a2326d1b8bec63fd4e29bbe2dfb8f8f075682be053ec2c7f6311564fe9.png)

From the graph, we see that the function increases without bound as $x$ decreases. Therefore,

$$
{lim}_{x\to -\infty }{(\frac{1}{32})}^{x}=\infty .
$$

Therefore, we conclude that

$$
{lim}_{x\to -\infty }{2}^{-5x}=\infty .
$$
